anomalies.observed: The servo signal section shows PWM1 feeding R3 into a node that then feeds R13 toward J3 pin 3, and PWM2 feeding R4 into a corresponding node that feeds R14 toward the TTL bus. A vertical wire joins the R3/R13 node to the R4/R14 node, so the two servo signal paths are tied together in the drawing rather than being selected only by the 0 Ω jumpers.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires independent PWM channels: '/PWM1 → J3 pin3, /PWM2 → J8 pin3' with R13/R14 left open, and R13/R14 only bridging J3 pin3 and J8 pin3 to the MAX3485 TTL bus in serial mode.

evidence.quote: Right-side servo section: PWM1 - R3 - node - R13 - J3 pin3; PWM2 - R4 - node - R14 - TTL; a vertical wire connects the two resistor junction nodes; annotation 'Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo'.
each servo header's signal pin gets its own independent 1 kΩ-buffered GPIO line (/PWM1 → J3 pin3, /PWM2 → J8 pin3) straight from the M5Stack bus.
R13, R14 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus

anomalies.impact: In PWM mode the pan and tilt signal paths are not independent; they are shorted together through the drawn vertical connection and/or one servo pin can be disconnected when the jumpers are open. In serial mode, if R3/R4 are populated, the M5Stack PWM GPIO nets may also be loaded onto the shared TTL servo bus.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to contain a servo-signal wiring anomaly: the R3/R13 and R4/R14 junctions are directly tied together, merging the two channels instead of leaving independent PWM paths and using R13/R14 only as serial-mode jumpers to the MAX3485 TTL bus.
